task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of June 30, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style reported feature about Foldline Maps' seasonal walking-map business and the work required to keep a printed product useful while routes and access information change.

facts.text: A June 2026 revision note records mapmaker Neri Saven removing an unconfirmed path connection from the next edition of the original Asterfen Footpath Map.
Foldline Maps is a two-person business selling printed local walking maps through shops and visitor centers.
The current print run is 2,000 copies at $1.20 each, producing a $2,400 print bill before fieldwork, design and other costs.
The listed retail price is $3.50, with participating retailers retaining 40%, or $1.40, of each sale.
Foldline receives $2.10 per retail sale under those terms, leaving 90 cents after the stated unit print cost but before other expenses.
Copies printed are not copies sold, and unsold editions can become outdated before their physical paper wears out.
The business checks proposed revisions against land-manager notices, direct permissions and its own recorded site observations.
A location omitted because access is unconfirmed is not thereby declared permanently closed or legally private.
The printed map identifies its revision month and directs readers to a dated corrections sheet available from stockists.
A corrections sheet can update information but cannot alter copies already in a customer's bag.
Saven said, "Paper does not need a signal, but it still needs a date."
Visitor-center worker Omi Harlen says some customers prefer a paper overview while using a phone for other travel information.
Harlen said, "People are not always choosing paper instead of a phone. Sometimes they want the two things to do different jobs."
The business has not measured a general decline in phone navigation or a universal preference for printed maps.
One planned revision concerns a footbridge under repair; the land manager has not announced its reopening date.
Foldline is holding space for an update rather than printing a guessed reopening promise.
The current records do not supply authority to settle disputed public-access rights or guarantee every route's future condition.
Retailers can return unopened bundles under negotiated terms, transferring some unsold-stock risk back to the publisher.
The business began with a hand-drawn festival-area leaflet in 2014 and now uses digital cartographic files for printing.
A planned larger regional edition remains a proposal, with no completed survey or committed print order.

forbidden_additions: All 2,000 copies sold, 90 cents is net profit or the map never needs updating
A settled access dispute, a guessed bridge reopening or a demonstrated rejection of phone navigation
